pr_title: Implement heartbeat in the Broadlink integration
pr_body:
<!--

## The problem
Some devices have a watchdog timer to ensure that the device remains connected to the cloud. They reboot when they don't receive heartbeats from the cloud for more than 3 minutes.

Lots of users want to block access to the internet for privacy reasons and this is causing their devices to reboot periodically. This PR comes to implement a local heartbeat to keep their devices awake even without access to the cloud.

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Send watchdog packets every two minutes to feed the watchdog timers of Broadlink devices. This will prevent them from rebooting when they cannot reach the cloud, so users can keep things local if they wish.

Credits to @marcan, who found the watchdog packet.

## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
Since 0.115.1 I have this error related to my Broadlink RM mini 3 showing in the logs at a rate of about 2 per hour.

> Error fetching device data: The device is offline

I have the device on a VLAN without internet access. I know it's trying to call home and while not able reconnects on my wifi on a 5/2 minutes period. Maybe it has something to do with this error.

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Configuration -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.115.1
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): 0.115.0
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core): HassOS 4.13 on a Pi3B+
- Integration causing this issue: Broadlink
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/broadlink/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

Config done with configuration flow.

```yaml
N/A
```

## Traceback/Error logs
<!--
  If you come across any trace or error logs, please provide them.
-->

```txt

```

## Additional information
comments: This is not a bug. We are polling your device for state now. If we miss an update, we show you an error message. If we miss 3 updates, your device is marked as unavailable.

Ok!
So the real bug is the broadlink firmware that reconnects for no "logical" reasons.

Too bad this device doesn't like to be isolated...

Thanks for clarifing

I do have the same "not" bug.
Showing this error on regular base
It would be an easy fix I guess to change the 3 bad poll to maybe 5 so the device gets back on the network before issuing an error.
I will add an extra attempt in the future. For now try to troubleshoot your connection. These messages mean that packets are being lost.

Like I said the problem is not my connection but the broadlink firmware that constantly reconnect to wifi when it cannot reach it's cloud...

The connection pattern is :
- about 5 minutes up
- reconnect
- about 2 minutes up
- reconnect

And this forever


Not much I can do other than letting it see the internet.

It looks annoying. What is the device type and firmware?

There is not much we can do here but add one more try. I don't think it will solve because it probably takes a while to reconnect.

Note that we are showing you an error message that tells you a real problem, so this is not a bug. We can make the update coordinator optional, so these messages will no longer appear if you don't want to.

Yes thats the right word.
In the beginning I thought it was realy an error the broadlink is not working.
So I tested the device every time and recognized it was still working.

Now it is only annoiyng there is a message at regular base

> It looks annoying. What is the device type and firmware?

It's a RM mini 3 and Home Assistant reports firmware 44057.

Maybe that will hide this annoyance.

## How to test?
### Option 1: Development container
Add these lines to the end of your Dockerfile.dev:
```bash
RUN pip3 install git+https://github.com/felipediel/python-broadlink.git@improve-scan --upgrade && pip3 install cryptography==2.9.2
```

### Option 2: Development environment
Activate your environment and install the update via shell command:
```bash
source venv/bin/activate
pip3 install git+https://github.com/felipediel/python-broadlink.git@improve-scan --upgrade
pip3 install cryptography==2.9.2
```

You can also update your production code using SSH add-on and Docker, but this is not recommended.

If you are talking about the error messages, people found out what is going on. When you block internet access the device reboots every 3 minutes, this is why the updates fail. So we are creating a mechanism to simulate a connection to the cloud and keep the device awake. It will take a while, we want to finish implementing device discovery first.

I can offer 3 workarounds for now:
1. Disable UPnP in your router's settings. It worked for me with 3 different routers, but I don't know if it is a universal solution. You can also...
2. Allow internet access. Or...
3. Install [this branch](https://github.com/mjg59/python-broadlink/pull/461) on a computer.
```bash
pip3 install git+https://github.com/felipediel/python-broadlink.git@keep-alive --upgrade
```
And run this script forever:
```python3
import broadlink as blk
import time

while True:
    blk.keep_alive("192.168.0.17", 80)  # Example device
    time.sleep(120)
```

review_comments: Why shouldn't we just create a pinger per config entry? Using a single manager goes against the grain of our architecture which relies on config entries. It also makes the implementation more complicated. This could just be a simple function that we subscribe and unsubscribe with the event listener.

In the previous implementation I was doing everything with a single job so as not to bomb the executor. Then I changed for some stupid reason during a clean up 😆

There are users with more than 10 devices and this method is called every 2 minutes, I think it makes sense to have a for loop with all the calls running inside a single executor job. How about?
How long does the ping take? I don't think we need to optimize it in that why unless we actually notice a problem.

@MartinHjelmare I think we need to differentiate and not use the same measure for all integrations. There are 2 types of integrations: the type who only have a couple of devices/platforms, and for those we should do everything at platform level, but then we have another type f.x. zwave, modbus and this one, which are "carrier" (in lack of a better word) for potentially a lot of devices/platform, performance in HA, and the network load matters.  I think our architecture needs to allow for both cases (just think of a sensor device with 32 sensors, that should surely not be pinged 32 times).

Having a loop inside a single executor job, is the perfect middle way in my mind, but I do not want to start a debate.
I'm not against optimizing it if we have done the calculations and think it's a problem.
